To configure a firewall to allow only SSH (port 22) and HTTP (port 80) traffic, you can use the following settings for `iptables` on a Linux system:

```
iptables -F
```

2. Set the default policy to DROP all incoming traffic:
```
iptable -P INPUT DROP
```

3. Allow established connections:
```
iptable -A INPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
```

4. Allow incoming SSH traffic:
```
iptable -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
```

5. Allow incoming HTTP traffic:
```
iptable -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT
```

6. Save the changes to ensure they are persistent across reboots:
```
save iptables
```

These rules will ensure that only SSH and HTTP traffic is allowed into the system while blocking all other incoming traffic.
